title: As Long As It Takes
logline: On a long, silent meditation retreat, a teacher meets each student for a few minutes every evening, trying to gauge, without ever quite asking, how deep they have gone.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Presence at the end of lives turns inward: a teacher's brief evening meetings on a silent retreat, trying to gauge how deep each student has gone.

thread_out.thread: From measuring stillness to keeping death close: a forest monk who sits at a village cemetery every morning before the village wakes.

requirements: A residential meditation centre willing to allow filming without disrupting the retreat
Students willing to be filmed and interviewed with full consent

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts describe calm, focused attention as something a person can train a little, moderately or to full mastery, and they link its depth to birth in the higher worlds. Those worlds have fewer ways of experiencing, not more: no smell, taste or touch, and no anger.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: සිතේ එකඟතාව ස්වල්ප ලෙස, මධ්‍යම ලෙස හෝ පූර්ණ ලෙස පුහුණු කළ හැකි බවත්, එහි ගැඹුර ඉහළ ලෝකවල උපතට සම්බන්ධ බවත්, එම ලෝකවල ගන්ධය, රසය, ස්පර්ශය හෝ තරහ නැති බැවින් අත්දැකීම් වැඩි නොව අඩු බවත් ග්‍රන්ථ කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches that rebirth into the fine-material (Brahma) worlds follows from meditative absorption (jhāna) not lost at death, and that a limited, moderate or excellent attainment, the last practised with the five masteries, leads to a lower or higher plane within the same tier. In the immaterial planes only the four mental aggregates exist, with no body at all. The texts add that the doors of smell, taste and touch are absent in the fine-material worlds, because birth there comes from meditation that turns away from sense pleasure, and that minds of aversion never arise there, since aversion is a hindrance to absorption.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Long silent hours, walking meditation on a forest path, and students waiting outside a door for a few minutes each evening. In the interviews a student says a little and the teacher listens for what lies underneath, so the viewer watches a living tradition trying, carefully, to gauge depth rather than reward effort. The retreat's narrowing of what reaches the senses gives the teaching a human, practising shape.

key_terms.en: the five masteries of an absorption
meditation through detachment from sense pleasures

lesson.caution: It is not a promise that meditation takes anyone to heaven, and a retreat's calm is not the absorption the texts describe; the texts also teach these worlds as real places of birth, so reading them as moods is an editorial choice.
lesson.builds_on: The last film sat with the senses of the dying; this one watches the living deliberately narrow their senses, and adds that the depth of a trained mind shapes what can follow.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
